To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the community structure of a graph can be used to improve the performance of graph matching algorithms.

(a) community degree vectors can be used to efficiently match graphs with community structure, (b) the percolation algorithm is not robust against imperfect matching as input, and (c) a novel percolating algorithm can be designed to use imperfect matching as input.

(i) community labels provide a useful form of side information to match correlated graphs, (ii) a simple algorithm based on community degree vectors harnesses the information in community labels, and (iii) an improved percolation algorithm can be used to efficiently match correlated graphs when an imperfect initial matching is provided as side information.

the following questions: (1) Can we use community structure to improve the performance of graph matching?
